column1: Minimum Absolute Difference in BST — return the minimum absolute difference between any two node values. Example: [4,2,6,1,3] → 1.
column2: PATTERN: In-order traversal (yields sorted sequence) with prev tracker. | INSIGHT: In a BST, the smallest difference is always between adjacent values in the in-order sequence. | STEPS: 1) prev=[None], ans=[inf]. 2) inorder(node): if not node: return; inorder(left); if prev[0] is not None: ans[0]=min(ans[0], node.val-prev[0]); prev[0]=node.val; inorder(right). 3) Return ans[0]. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(h). | PITFALL: Brute pair-check is O(n²) — exploiting BST order is the win.

column1: Kth Smallest Element in a BST — return the kth smallest value (1-indexed). Example: [3,1,4,null,2], k=1 → 1; [5,3,6,2,4,null,null,1], k=3 → 3.
column2: PATTERN: Iterative in-order with stack, stop at the kth pop. | INSIGHT: In-order yields sorted; just pop k times. | STEPS: 1) stack=[]; cur=root. 2) Loop: while cur: stack.append(cur); cur=cur.left. cur=stack.pop(); k-=1; if k==0: return cur.val; cur=cur.right. | TIME/SPACE: O(h+k) / O(h). | PITFALL: Don't traverse the whole tree — early-exit on k==0.

column1: Validate Binary Search Tree — return True if a tree is a valid BST (left subtree all strictly less, right subtree all strictly greater, recursively). Example: [2,1,3] → True; [5,1,4,null,null,3,6] → False.
column2: PATTERN: Recursion with min/max bounds. | INSIGHT: Each node must lie strictly inside its inherited (low, high) range — local parent comparisons are not enough. | STEPS: valid(node, low, high): 1) If not node: True. 2) If node.val<=low or node.val>=high: False. 3) Return valid(left, low, node.val) and valid(right, node.val, high). 4) Call valid(root, -inf, inf). | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(h). | PITFALL: Just comparing node to its immediate children is wrong — a deep right descendant could break the invariant.
